about.title: About Marichoo
about.content:
Marija Knezić Banožić aka "Marichoo" is an illustrator, graphic designer & artist with a quirky mind, endless flow of creative ideas & versatile skills!

A note from Marija

Hi! I come from Croatia, where I studied at the Academy of Fine Arts and Faculty of Humanities. During my studies I discovered my love for illustration.

In Croatia and Germany I worked as an illustrator & graphic designer and was very lucky to work with some very prominent clients, such as Playboy, Brigitte, Beck’s, Podravka and Henschel.

My biggest inspiration comes from everyday life, which, seen from another perspective, can be magical, beautiful and absurd. My great love and source of inspiration is also medieval art, full of detail, life and humour. I start each project with a lot of writing; writing down ideas, thoughts, keywords… That helps me to come to the final idea and start making sketches.

I mostly do my illustrations on iPad, using the Procreate app. My favourite subject is people, I enjoy studying and drawing human bodies, faces, movements and expressions.

I would describe my style as figurative, clean, graphic & colourful. I wish you a nice day and have fun exploring my website!

See my portfolio.

Art Teacher, August Cesarec Primary School
Krapina, Croatia 2026 - ongoing

I teach art to primary school students, helping them discover drawing, painting and design, and encouraging them to find their own creative voice.

Arts & Culture Manager, Kajkaviana
Donja Stubica, Croatia 2023 - 2026

Kajkaviana is a cultural association in Donja Stubica dedicated to preserving and promoting the Kajkavian language, heritage and culture of the region.

I planned and managed cultural and arts programmes, including exhibitions, workshops and events. I also designed the visual materials for them: posters, publications and social media.

Graphic Designer, Henschel
Darmstadt, Germany 2019 - 2023

Henschel is a German fashion & lifestyle company with fashion stores located in Darmstadt, Heidelberg, Michelstadt and Lübeck.

I worked closely with the social media manager and the marketing manager to create newsletters, social media ads, articles, website updates and such. I also designed many print materials such as posters, brochures, flyers & POS materials. I was also responsible for Gegenüber, another brand of Henschel, for all things regarding design & visual identity. I also did the rebranding of the brand / corporate visual identity.

Graphic Designer & Illustrator, Augustanec Group
Zagreb, Croatia 2017 - 2018

Augustanec Group is the biggest Croatian company that designs and produces souvenirs. It produces souvenirs for most of Europe.

My responsibilities were illustration and design of the souvenirs. I learned a lot about the processes of manufacturing, working with different materials and product design.

Graphic Designer, BBDO advertising agency
Zagreb, Croatia 2014 - 2016

Working with major Croatian and international brands, such as: Molson Coors (Staropramen, Stella Artois, Beck’s, Ožujsko), Wrigley, Vienna Insurance Group, Podravka, Lactalis Group, Dukat, Plazma, ...

I have worked on everything related to graphic design for print: flyers, posters, brochures, packages, magazine ads and POS materials. I’ve also worked for online: designed web banners, social media ads and designed and prepared files for animation.

Working in a dynamic agency environment, I've gained valuable experience in how to tackle versatile tasks simultaneously and under tight deadlines.

projects.title: Campaign 2 for Plazma
projects.summary: Proposals by Marichoo for “Dilemmas”, a brand campaign for the Serbian biscuit brand Plazma, with art direction and graphic design.
projects.content:
These are the proposals of visuals for the brand campaign for Plazma, famous Serbian biscuit brand. I was responsible for art direction and graphic design. (After I left the agency and the campaign was about to begin, the final designs were slightly modified.)The name of the campaign is “Dilemmas” as the Plazma biscuits can be consumed both grounded or whole, can be used for making desserts or eaten the way they are....
There are three headlines and each address a different dilemma. The first one says: “Nutritious or sweet?”. Second one : “With a fork or with a spoon?” meaning: to eat something solid or something liquid. Finally, the third headline says: “Kid’s way or mom’s way?”
I used the biscuit as the main visual element and added the illustrated elements to correspond to the headline. The result is eye- catching, simple yet fun design that unites headline, visual and brand.

Credits:
agency: BBDO Zagreb
graphic designer: Marija Knezić Marichoo
copywriter: Miro Peric
photos, illustrations: Plazma, Shutterstock

image.alt: Plazma biscuit ad on red: two biscuits drawn as a fork and a spoon, asking “Suho ili na žlicu?” (dry or with a spoon?)

projects.title: Proposal for design visuals for Vienna Insurance Group
projects.summary: A key visual proposal by Marichoo for a Vienna Insurance Group life insurance campaign: “You are his superhero. So do what heroes do. Protect him.”
projects.content:
This is a proposal for the design of the key visual for for life insurance campaign for prominent Vienna Insurance Group. I was responsible for art direction and graphic design.
The motto of the campaign says: “ You are his superhero. So do what heroes do. Protect him.”
I wanted the design to follow the motto and that explains the choice of the photo and font, which is somewhat of cut-out, kid’s style.
The red colour corresponds with the official brand’s colour. The white frame gives the final touch to the design; it stabilises the composition and the cape that goes over it
make for a playful detail.

Credits:
agency: BBDO Zagreb
graphic designer: Marija Knezić Marichoo
copywriter: Tino Kera
photos: Shutterstock

image.alt: Vienna Insurance Group poster “Ti si njegov superheroj”: a father and son in red capes running across a field

projects.title: 36 Mountains, illustration festival
projects.summary: Marichoo’s work for 36 Mountains, an international illustration festival where each artist fills a 1.8-metre concertina notebook using only black.
projects.content:
36 Mountains is an international festival dedicated to illustration. The goal of the festival is to bring illustration and drawing closer to the public, and also to present the best of the domestic and global illustration scene.

1,80 meter long concertina notebooks designed specifically for this project are given to each artist that was chosen by the jury. The artists are free to express themselves how ever they want, the only rule they need to follow is: use only black! 

The main festival exhibition is showing the notebooks that each artist has done.

image.alt: Illuminated concertina notebook drawn in black ink with acrobatic figures in striped swimsuits, for the 36 Mountains illustration festival

projects.title: Slap & Stick
projects.summary: Slap & Stick is a series of art magnets by Marichoo that turn fridges, radiators and any iron object into a piece of art.
projects.content:
Slap & Stick is a series of art magnets.
The idea of this project is that everyone can take this art magnets and turn their refrigerators, radiators, washing machines or every iron object, into a piece of art.
Hand drawn motifs are printed on a sticker which is then put on magnetic foil and cut. Magnets depict quirky motifs, such as internal organs, pig’s head, wings, lollipops…. 


Photos by Igor Dugandžić.

image.alt: Slap & Stick art magnets on a radiator: three Russian nesting dolls and a gun with a “bang” burst

projects.title: Homepages
projects.summary: Homepages is a series of works by Marichoo made of metal boards and magnets, shaped like children’s worksheets for dressing up a paper doll.
projects.content: Homepages is a series of works made of metal board and magnets. Each work, by its visual form, resembles to children’s worksheets. It has two “pages”. On the left one there are magnets- bordered with dashed line as in girl’s worksheet for dressing up a paper doll. On the right page is a depiction of an interior. Viewer can pick each motif from the left side and put it on the depicted interior on the right. All works from Homepage series (as well as my projects in which I have used magnets) interwork together; one can take a motif from another work and put it on these “pages”, thus making somewhat surreal and ever-changing compositions.

image.alt: Homepages artwork “Bathroom”: a metal board with magnets of legs, a rubber duck, soap and shampoo for dressing up a drawn bath scene

projects.title: Play & Go
projects.summary: Play & Go is an interactive artwork by Marichoo: a 140 × 180 cm metal board with magnets that can be moved into countless compositions.
projects.content:
Play & Go“ is an artwork made out of metal board (dimensions 140x 180 cm) and many various motifs- magnets. One can move magnets all over the board, thus making dynamic composition with countless variations.
Motifs from the „Play & Go” can as well be arranged as independent compositions on every metal surface. It is interactive and fun.

Viewer can move magnets on the board and thus make dynamic composition in countless combinations.

Each magnet can be extracted, put on any metal surface thus making an individual art piece.

image.alt: Play & Go magnetic artwork detail: line-drawn nesting dolls, hands, a banana and a bald head on a pink metal board

projects.title: Swiss Knife for Women or Woman’s Survival Kit
projects.summary: A poster by Marichoo about gender stereotypes: the Swiss knife as a symbol of manhood, and a woman’s purse as her survival kit.
projects.content:
This poster came out as a result of thinking on gender stereotypes. Swiss knife is, because of it’s practicality, efficiency and usefulness,
a symbol of manhood and therefore “must-have” for every man. Woman’s equivalent is her purse; full of things which purpose men don’t understand, but which make “woman’s survival kit”

image.alt: Poster “Swiss Knife for Women or Woman’s Survival Kit”: a Swiss knife whose tools are a lipstick, a stiletto, a comb, a phone and a vibrator

projects.title: Backpack for Croats and Everyone Who Feels Like One
projects.summary: A student art installation by Marichoo: a cardboard model of a backpack in the shape of a cross, with a manual for this mock-up product.
projects.content:
This is a very old student project of mine (that's why the poor quality of the photos).

The work represent a mock-up product, mock-up in every way.

The artwork consists of a cardboard model of a backpack in the shape of a cross and accompanying manual. In the manual, the “product” is described and different models of backpack for different profiles of people are presented. Each model is further explained with additional descriptions of it’s parts. The backpack is exhibited on a mannequin which accentuate the illusion that this is a real product.

From the manual introduction:
“It is common knowledge that Croats have the hardest time. Every Croat “carries his cross”. So if you are a Croat or just feel like one, then “Backpack for Croats and Everyone Who Feels Like One” is a solution for you! Why wouldn’t you put all your worries and troubles that burden your shoulders into this backpack and make your life easier? Along with the basic model, we offer you a model for students, retired, business people and veterans, because troubles don’t choose! Each backpack is ergonomically shaped to ease you carrying the burden of life, while it’s basic model leaves you space to express your personality and carry your miseries with style!”

image.alt: Child mannequin wearing a cardboard backpack in the shape of a cross, student art installation

projects.title: Key Visual for Dukat Campaign
projects.summary: A key visual proposal by Marichoo for Dukat, the biggest Croatian dairy brand, for a campaign inviting children to draw their perfect family breakfast.
projects.content:
This is the design proposition of the campaign key visual for the biggest Croatian dairy brand named Dukat. I was responsible for graphic design. The campaign was actually a call for entries to competition for children to draw their perfect family breakfast. (The best of the drawings would end up on packagings of the milk as a limited edition. )
Campaign was about children drawing their perfect family breakfast, therefore the childlike font that looks like it was made with paint brush. To emphasise the theme even more and to add playfulness to the somewhat sterile photo, I literally added the illustration of the breakfast.


Credits:
agency: BBDO Zagreb
graphic designer: Marija Knezić Marichoo
copywriter: Miro Peric

image.alt: Dukat key visual “Dječje ruke za zajedničke trenutke”: a girl laughing at breakfast with her parents, beside a child’s drawing of cereal and milk
